name: Nayapul
blurb: The old roadhead on the Pokhara to Baglung highway where most southern Annapurna treks used to begin. Jeep tracks now run on up both valleys, so many groups only pass through.
tip: Buses for Nayapul leave from Pokhara's Baglung bus park; a taxi or shared jeep saves about an hour.

name: Birethanti
blurb: A riverside village where the Bhurungdi Khola meets the Modi Khola, twenty minutes beyond Nayapul. Permits are checked at the bridge before the trails to Ghorepani and Ghandruk divide.

name: Tikhedhunga
blurb: A string of lodges beside the Bhurungdi Khola at the foot of the Ulleri staircase. It is the usual first night on the walk to Ghorepani, and jeeps from Pokhara come this far, with Hile just below.

name: Ulleri
blurb: A Magar village stacked up a steep hillside, reached from the river by more than 3,000 stone steps. The first views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli open up from its upper lodges.
tip: Climb the steps early, before the sun reaches them. There is tea and water every twenty minutes or so.

name: Banthanti
blurb: A handful of lodges in oak and rhododendron forest between Ulleri and Ghorepani, used mostly as a lunch stop. Do not confuse it with the Banthanti on the Ghorepani to Tadapani trail.

name: Ghorepani
blurb: A large lodge village on a forested saddle below Poon Hill, where the trails from Nayapul, Tatopani and Tadapani meet. Nearly everyone here is up before dawn for the walk to the viewpoint.
tip: Lodges in the upper part of the village are closer to the Poon Hill path and have the better mountain views.

name: Poon Hill
blurb: A grassy summit with a viewing tower, 45 minutes to an hour above Ghorepani. At sunrise the skyline runs from Dhaulagiri across the Kali Gandaki gorge to Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
tip: A small entry fee is collected at a booth on the path. Bring cash, a head torch and a warm layer for the wait at the top.

name: Tadapani
blurb: A cluster of lodges in a forest clearing on the ridge between Ghorepani and Ghandruk. On a clear morning Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre stand right in front of the dining rooms.
tip: The few lodges fill quickly in October and April. Arrive by early afternoon or have your guide phone ahead.

name: Ghandruk
blurb: One of the largest Gurung villages in Nepal, its slate-roofed stone houses stepping down a hillside opposite Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. A road now reaches the lower edge of the village.
tip: Stay in the old upper village rather than beside the jeep stand, and leave half an hour for the small Gurung museum.

name: Kimche
blurb: The bus and jeep stop on the road below Ghandruk, about an hour's climb on stone steps from the village centre. Vehicles from Pokhara come by way of Nayapul and Syauli Bazaar.

name: Komrong Danda
blurb: A ridge-top tea stop about an hour above Ghandruk on the way to Chhomrong. From here the trail drops steeply to the Kimrong Khola before climbing again.

name: Chhomrong
blurb: The last permanent village on the way to the Annapurna Sanctuary, spread down a steep hillside facing Annapurna South. Beyond it there are only lodges, and prices rise at every stop.
tip: The checkpoint here records everyone going up. Ask the staff about snow and avalanche conditions above Deurali.

name: Jhinu Danda
blurb: A small lodge village on a spur below Chhomrong, known for the hot spring pools beside the Modi Khola about twenty minutes' walk downhill. A long suspension bridge links it to the jeep track.
tip: Take a towel and sandals down to the springs and leave valuables at the lodge.

name: Sinuwa
blurb: Lodges on the forested ridge across the Chhomrong Khola from Chhomrong, at the start of the Modi Khola gorge. Lodges above here serve no meat, out of respect for the belief that the Sanctuary is sacred.

name: Bamboo
blurb: A damp clearing of lodges in thick bamboo forest on the floor of the Modi Khola gorge. It gets little sun and is the usual overnight stop on the way down from base camp.

name: Dovan
blurb: Three or four lodges in the forest about an hour above Bamboo. Sleeping here rather than at Bamboo shortens the next day's climb to Deurali.

name: Himalaya
blurb: Two lodges wedged into the narrowest part of the gorge between Dovan and Deurali. The cliffs keep the place in shade for most of the day.

name: Deurali
blurb: The last lodges before the avalanche-prone stretch of the Modi Khola gorge and the usual night stop before the Sanctuary. The forest ends just below; ahead the valley is open rock and grass.
tip: Ask the lodge owners each morning whether the main trail or the detour is in use, and leave early.

name: Machhapuchhre Base Camp
blurb: A group of lodges at the entrance to the Annapurna Sanctuary, under the north-west face of Machhapuchhre. The peak is sacred and closed to climbers, so the name is a courtesy and no expedition uses it.
tip: If you have a headache here, sleep at this height and walk up to Annapurna Base Camp for sunrise instead.

name: Annapurna Base Camp
blurb: A cluster of lodges on the moraine of the South Annapurna Glacier, ringed by Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre. At sunrise the light comes down the 8,091 m face directly above.
tip: Nights are below freezing in every season. Rent a warm sleeping bag in Pokhara rather than relying on lodge blankets.

name: Kande
blurb: A roadside bazaar on the Pokhara to Baglung highway, about an hour's drive from Lakeside. It is the usual starting point for Australian Camp and the Mardi Himal ridge.

name: Australian Camp
blurb: A grassy hilltop with lodges and camping lawns about an hour above Kande. It looks straight at the Annapurna range and is a popular overnight walk from Pokhara even without going further.

name: Pothana
blurb: A lodge village on the forested ridge between Dhampus and Pitam Deurali. Permits are inspected at the conservation area checkpoint here.

name: Pitam Deurali
blurb: A small saddle with a few lodges where the Mardi Himal trail leaves the main path to Landruk and turns north up the ridge. It is the last stop with a choice of lodges before Forest Camp.

name: Forest Camp
blurb: Basic lodges in a clearing in dense oak and rhododendron forest on the Mardi Himal ridge. There are no views; it is simply the first place to stop on the long forest section.

name: Low Camp
blurb: Lodges at the upper edge of the forest on the Mardi Himal ridge, with the first close view of Machhapuchhre up the valley. The steep trail down to Siding leaves the ridge here.

name: Badal Danda
blurb: A few lodges on the open ridge above the tree line between Low Camp and High Camp. The name means cloud hill, and by midday it usually lives up to it.

name: Mardi Himal High Camp
blurb: The highest lodges on the Mardi Himal ridge and the base for the dawn climb to the viewpoint and base camp. Rooms are basic, water is limited and the ridge is exposed to wind.
tip: Beds run out in October and November. Book through your guide or arrive before lunch.

name: Mardi Himal Upper Viewpoint
blurb: A prayer-flagged knoll on the narrow ridge above High Camp where most trekkers stop. Machhapuchhre is only a few kilometres away, with Annapurna South and Hiunchuli across the Modi Khola.

name: Mardi Himal Base Camp
blurb: A marker on the ridge beyond the Upper Viewpoint, quoted at about 4,500 m. It is a trekkers' high point below Mardi Himal rather than a climbing base, and there is no shelter.

name: Siding
blurb: A farming village in the Mardi Khola valley at the foot of the steep descent from Low Camp. Homestays and lodges serve lunch, and jeeps leave from here for Pokhara.

name: Dhampus
blurb: A Gurung village on a ridge above the Seti valley with a long view of the Annapurna range. It can be reached by road or by a short climb from Phedi and is an alternative start for Mardi Himal.

name: Landruk
blurb: A Gurung village on the east side of the Modi Khola, facing Ghandruk across the valley. It lies on the old Dhampus route to Annapurna Base Camp and on one of the ways down from the Mardi Himal ridge.

name: Dobato
blurb: Two or three simple lodges in a high clearing on the ridge north-west of Tadapani. It is the base for the short dawn climb to the Muldai viewpoint.
tip: Lodge space is limited. In peak season have your guide call ahead from Tadapani.

name: Muldai Viewpoint
blurb: A bare hilltop about half an hour above Dobato, higher than Poon Hill and far quieter. The view takes in Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre.

name: Bayeli
blurb: A community lodge on a grassy ridge between Dobato and Khopra Danda, used as a lunch stop or a quiet overnight halt. Herders bring buffalo and sheep up here in summer.

name: Chistibang
blurb: A community lodge in the forest below Khopra Danda, at roughly 3,000 m. It breaks the climb to the ridge whether you come across from Bayeli or up from Swanta.

name: Khopra Danda
blurb: A grassy spur high above the Kali Gandaki with a community lodge on its crest. Dhaulagiri stands directly across the gorge and Annapurna South rises close behind the lodge.
tip: The community lodge is small. Reserve through a guide or agency in October, November and April.

name: Khayer Lake
blurb: A small sacred lake with a shrine below the west flank of Annapurna South, reached by a long day walk from Khopra Danda. Its height is quoted anywhere from 4,500 to 4,660 m and there is no shelter on the way.

name: Swanta
blurb: A quiet Magar farming village across the Ghar Khola valley from Chitre, with a community lodge and a few family guesthouses. It is the usual stop between Khopra Danda and Ghorepani.

name: Chitre
blurb: A scattered village on the trail between Ghorepani and Tatopani, where the path to Swanta and Khopra Danda turns off. Its lodges face Dhaulagiri.

name: Galeshwor
blurb: A small bazaar and temple town on the Kali Gandaki a few kilometres north of Beni. The Mohare Danda community trail starts across the suspension bridge here.

name: Banskharka
blurb: A Magar farming village among terraces and orange trees above the Kali Gandaki, with the first community lodge on the Mohare Danda trail.

name: Nangi
blurb: A Magar village known for its school and for the wireless internet project that Mahabir Pun started here. The village runs the community lodge, and the income supports the school and health post.

name: Mohare Danda
blurb: A forested hilltop with a community lodge and a clearing that looks out to Dhaulagiri, the Annapurnas and Machhapuchhre. It is slightly higher than Poon Hill and sees a fraction of the visitors.

name: Danda Kharka
blurb: A community lodge on a pasture ridge in the rhododendron forest below Mohare Danda, on the way down to Tikot. It makes a short, easy stage after the summit morning.

name: Tikot
blurb: A compact Magar village of stone houses on a spur high above the Kali Gandaki, with a community homestay and a clear view of Dhaulagiri.

name: Tiplyang
blurb: A roadside settlement on the Beni to Jomsom road, north of Galeshwor. The Mohare Danda community trail ends here, and buses and jeeps run down to Beni and Pokhara.

name: Bhulbhule
blurb: A riverside village a short drive north of Besisahar where the Annapurna Circuit used to begin on foot. A few walkers still start here to follow the old trail up the Marsyangdi, away from the road.

name: Tal
blurb: The first village of Manang district, on a flat stretch of the Marsyangdi valley floor beneath a waterfall. It is a common stop for those who still walk the lower part of the Annapurna Circuit.

name: Shikha
blurb: A large Magar village strung along the hillside between Tatopani and Ghorepani. It is the usual lunch or overnight stop on that 1,700 m climb, with Dhaulagiri in view to the north-west.

name: Timang
blurb: A small village on a shelf above the Marsyangdi gorge with a wide view back to Manaslu. It is a common lunch stop between Dharapani and Chame.

name: Koto
blurb: A roadside village twenty minutes before Chame, where the Nar Khola gorge joins the Marsyangdi. The police post here checks Nar Phu restricted-area permits.

name: Chame
blurb: The headquarters of Manang district, with shops, a bank, a health post and small hot springs across the river. Many trekkers now begin walking here after a jeep ride from Besisahar.
tip: The cash machine is often empty or offline. Carry your money from Kathmandu or Pokhara.

name: Bhratang
blurb: An apple farm with a lodge and café in pine forest about two hours above Chame. Just beyond it the curved rock wall of Paungda Danda rises some 1,500 m from the river.

name: Dhikur Pokhari
blurb: A row of lodges on a forested bench above the Marsyangdi, used as a lunch stop. The low trail to Lower Pisang and the path to Upper Pisang divide just beyond.

name: Upper Pisang
blurb: A stone village on the hillside north of the river, with a monastery at its top and a direct view of Annapurna II. It is the start of the high trail to Manang through Ghyaru and Ngawal.

name: Lower Pisang
blurb: The newer half of Pisang, on the valley floor beside the road. It has more lodges than the upper village and is the start of the low, easier route to Manang through Humde.

name: Ghyaru
blurb: An old stone village on a terrace about 400 m above the valley floor, reached by a long set of switchbacks. Annapurna II, III and IV line up across the valley.

name: Ngawal
blurb: A large traditional village on the high route between Pisang and Manang, and the first village on the descent from the Kang La. It is higher than Manang, so a night here helps with acclimatization.

name: Humde
blurb: A village beside Manang's airstrip on the valley floor. Scheduled flights are rare, but it sits on the road and the low route, and jeeps down the valley can be arranged here.

name: Braga
blurb: A village half an hour before Manang, built in tiers below a monastery that is among the oldest in the district. The trail to Ice Lake starts here.

name: Manang
blurb: The main village of the upper Marsyangdi and the standard acclimatization stop before the Thorong La. It has shops, bakeries and a Himalayan Rescue Association aid post staffed in the main seasons.
tip: Spend at least two nights, three if you came up by jeep, and go to the aid post's afternoon altitude talk in season.

name: Gangapurna Lake
blurb: A milky green lake at the snout of the Gangapurna Glacier, across the river from Manang. It is half an hour's walk from the village and the start of the climb to the Chongkor viewpoint.

name: Praken Gompa
blurb: A small hermitage built against the cliff about 400 m above Manang. The climb takes around two hours and makes a useful acclimatization walk, with the Annapurna range spread out behind you.

name: Ice Lake
blurb: A pair of small lakes on a high shelf above Braga, about 1,100 m above the valley floor. The steep climb is the hardest of the Manang acclimatization hikes and looks across to the whole Annapurna range.
tip: Allow six to seven hours for the round trip from Manang and turn back if a headache builds.

name: Gunsang
blurb: A few lodges on the hillside an hour and a half above Manang, where the trail turns north into the side valley that leads to the Thorong La. A good tea stop on the way to Yak Kharka.

name: Yak Kharka
blurb: A line of lodges on open pasture above the tree line, the usual first night after Manang. Blue sheep often graze on the slopes around it.

name: Ledar
blurb: A small group of lodges about an hour beyond Yak Kharka. Sleeping here instead shortens the next morning's walk to Thorong Phedi.

name: Thorong Phedi
blurb: The lodges at the foot of the climb to the Thorong La, set under cliffs beside the river. Most trekkers sleep here and start for the pass between four and five in the morning.
tip: If you feel unwell here, go back down to Ledar or Yak Kharka. Do not continue to High Camp.

name: Thorong High Camp
blurb: A large lodge about an hour above Thorong Phedi. Sleeping here shortens the pass day, but at around 4,850 m it is a cold and often sleepless night for anyone not well acclimatized.

name: Thorong La
blurb: The pass between Manang and Mustang and the high point of the Annapurna Circuit, marked by prayer flags and a small tea hut in season. Wind builds from mid-morning, so parties cross early.
tip: Aim to be on top by nine or ten. Turn back if cloud and snow close in before you reach the pass.

name: Khangsar
blurb: The last permanent village on the way to Tilicho Lake, set above the gorge west of Manang. A rough road now reaches it from Manang.

name: Shree Kharka
blurb: Two or three lodges on a grassy shelf below the cliffs, about an hour and a half beyond Khangsar. It is the last stop before the landslide slopes on the way to Tilicho Base Camp.

name: Tilicho Base Camp
blurb: A few large lodges on the valley floor below the moraine wall that hides Tilicho Lake. Everyone leaves before dawn for the climb, and rooms are short in peak season.
tip: Have your guide reserve beds a day ahead. Late arrivals in October sometimes sleep in the dining room.

name: Tilicho Lake
blurb: A large glacial lake below the ice wall of Tilicho Peak, usually quoted at 4,919 m. The trail ends at a viewpoint and seasonal tea hut above the south-east shore; the lake is frozen through winter and into spring.

name: Meta
blurb: A group of lodges on a grassy shelf above the Nar Khola gorge and the first night's stop after Koto. It began as a winter settlement for the people of Nar.

name: Kyang
blurb: A winter settlement of Phu villagers on a plateau above the river, between Meta and Phu. Ruined stone houses here were once occupied by Khampa refugees from Tibet.

name: Phu
blurb: A fortified hilltop village of stacked stone houses at the head of the Phu Khola, home to a few dozen families of Tibetan origin. Tashi Lhakhang monastery sits on the hill across the river.

name: Nar Phedi
blurb: A monastery guesthouse beside the river below Nar, run by the resident nuns. Trekkers sleep in simple rooms, eat in the monastery kitchen and are welcome at the evening prayers.

name: Nar
blurb: A large farming village on a sunny shelf below Pisang Peak, livelier than Phu, with barley fields, several small monasteries and a few lodges. It is the last village before the Kang La.

name: Kang La Phedi
blurb: Yak pastures at the foot of the Kang La, two to three hours above Nar. A basic tea house may open in the main seasons, and groups sometimes sleep or camp here to shorten the pass day.

name: Kang La
blurb: The pass linking Nar with Ngawal in the Manang valley. The Nar side is a long, gradual climb; the Manang side drops steeply over scree, with the Annapurna range and Tilicho Peak ahead.

name: Jharkot
blurb: A fortified village on a ridge half an hour below Muktinath, with a red monastery and the ruins of an old fort. It is quieter than Ranipauwa and about 200 m lower, which makes for an easier night.

name: Eklebhatti
blurb: A few lodges on the bank of the Kali Gandaki between Jomsom and Kagbeni, where the direct route to Muktinath leaves the valley floor. The name means lone teahouse.

name: Lubra
blurb: A small village in the Panda Khola side valley and one of the few places in Nepal where the Bon religion is still practised. It lies on the trail that avoids the road between Muktinath and Jomsom.

name: Thini
blurb: An old Thakali village on a terrace across the river from Jomsom, older than the town itself. It makes a short walk away from the road and is on the way to Dhumba Lake.

name: Dhumba Lake
blurb: A small green lake below Nilgiri that local Buddhists hold sacred, about an hour and a half from Jomsom by way of Thini. A monastery stands on the ridge above it.

name: Tukuche
blurb: A former salt-trading town of large Thakali merchant houses with carved wooden windows. It has monasteries, a fruit distillery and several good lodges, and is far quieter than Jomsom.

name: Larjung
blurb: A village on the broad gravel bed of the Kali Gandaki below the east face of Dhaulagiri, with Kobang next door. The long side trip to the Dhaulagiri Icefall viewpoint starts here.

name: Kalopani
blurb: A lodge village in pine forest with peaks on every side: Dhaulagiri, Tukuche Peak, the Nilgiris and Annapurna I. Lete is twenty minutes further down the road.

name: Lete
blurb: A spread-out village just below Kalopani, with lodges along the road and a side trail to Titi Lake. Either village works as the night stop between Marpha and Tatopani.

name: Ghasa
blurb: The southernmost Thakali village, at the point where the valley narrows into the gorge and pine gives way to broadleaf forest. Permits are checked at the conservation area post here.

name: Dana
blurb: A village of old houses and orange trees in the deepest part of the Kali Gandaki gorge, about an hour and a half above Tatopani. The Rupse waterfall is a short way upstream.
